prompts.generator:
Generate a reachable intermediate Sokoban state from the CURRENT board in the final user message. The earlier input/output pairs are verified training transitions with measured scale labels; use them to interpret the scale, never copy their boards. A subgoal is a complete future board, including the player's final position.
Symbols: # wall, - empty floor, . empty goal, $ box on floor, * box on goal, @ player on floor, + player on goal. Walls and goal locations never change. Coordinates, when used, are zero-based [row,column]; UP decreases row, DOWN increases row, LEFT decreases column, RIGHT increases column.
Construct the board by following these steps internally. First identify the player's cell, all boxes, and the fixed wall/goal map. Choose a short legal sequence of single-cell moves, no longer than the stated action cap L, towards a useful intermediate position. Walking to the correct side of a box is useful even when no box has moved yet. Use the requested scale as defined below; it does not override legal movement.
For each move, inspect the adjacent destination. A wall blocks the move. An empty floor or goal allows the player to move there. If the destination contains a box, the cell one further in the SAME direction must be inside the board and contain neither a wall nor another box: move that box one cell forward and move the player into the box's old cell. Otherwise the move is blocked and must not be used to construct a changed state. Never pull, jump, teleport, move a box without its pushing player, or push two boxes. Avoid pushing a box into a non-goal corner. Continue from the updated positions after every move, not from the original positions.
After planning, render the resulting positions onto the ORIGINAL fixed wall/goal map. Every vacated cell becomes . if it is a goal, otherwise -. Render a box as * on a goal or $ on floor; render the single player as + on a goal or @ on floor. In particular, remove the old @ or + when moving the player and remove the old $ or * when moving a box. Preserve all unchanged cells exactly.
Check the complete rendered board: same dimensions, identical wall and goal locations, exactly the original number of boxes counting both $ and *, and exactly one player counting both @ and +. It must differ from the current board and from the other proposed boards. Select a purposeful reachable endpoint, not an imagined solved arrangement. If no distinct endpoint can be constructed, return an empty subgoals array. Return only the requested JSON containing complete board rows; keep the internal plan out of the output.
